title: Drime multipart uploads ignore configured folder ID and land in the root directory
body: I connected Drime to rclone using a specific folder ID. Small files around 5–10 MB upload into that folder, but a large file around 1 GB fails verification and appears in the Drime root directory instead. It should be uploaded into the configured “Rclone” folder. I downloaded rclone again after the linked update and reconfigured the remote several times, but the same thing keeps happening.

symptoms_visible: Files around 5–10 MB upload into my configured Drime folder, but a large file around 1 GB fails verification and appears in the Drime root directory instead.
Downloading rclone again after the earlier update and reconfiguring the remote several times did not change where large files are uploaded.
N0.label: N0 large Drime uploads placed in root

symptoms_visible: With rclone v1.74.0, ocean.mp4 reaches 100%, appears in the Drime root directory, and ends with “multi-thread copy: failed to find object after copy: object not found.”
N1_x.label: N1_x v1.74.0 update aftermath

symptoms_visible: The provided test build uploaded the large file under the folder ID I configured instead of placing it in the Drime root.
My first upload into a folder inside that configured folder stopped with a Cloudflare 520 response, but running it again succeeded.
N2.label: N2 folder placement fixed in first test build

symptoms_visible: The latest provided branch worked flawlessly with my test files.
N3.label: N3 cumulative branch verified by reporter

symptoms_visible: Large multipart uploads using the verified fix are placed under my configured Drime folder instead of appearing in the root directory.
N_terminal.label: terminal folder placement resolved

solution.intent: Update to the newly released rclone v1.74.0 and retry the same large Drime upload.
solution.concrete_example: Install the just-released v1.74.0, use the same Drime remote and folder ID, and retry the large file.

edges.comment: Thread c0-c1, reporter's system only: the reporter installed v1.74.0 and reproduced the original placement problem. The completed upload still appeared in root and verification ended with “failed to find object after copy,” so updating to v1.74.0 alone was falsified.

question_patterns: Please try the provided test build with the same Drime remote and large file. Where does the uploaded file appear?
Can you test this beta build and tell me whether the large upload lands under your configured folder ID?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It worked for the folder ID I configured. I also created a folder inside it and tried that destination: the first run stopped with a Cloudflare 520 error, but when I ran it again, that upload worked too.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The test build still uploads the large file into the Drime root and ends with the same object-not-found error.
The configured-folder upload works, but the first nested-folder attempt gets a temporary Cloudflare 520 and succeeds on retry.

edges.comment: Thread c2-c4, reporter's system only: the maintainer supplied a pre-landing branch build after analyzing the multipart path handling. The reporter's raw result was that placement under the configured folder ID worked. The nested-folder Cloudflare 520 was transient and is not treated as the cause of the original root-placement bug.

question_patterns: Can you test the latest branch build with your files and report what happens?
Please retry your test set using the latest provided build and tell me whether the uploads complete correctly.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Worked flawlessly! I tried it with these files and the uploads completed successfully.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The latest branch still puts large uploads in the root directory instead of my configured folder.
The latest branch works with the same files, but transfer speeds vary between runs.

edges.comment: Thread c26-c28, reporter's system only: the reporter tested the latest cumulative branch and reported that it worked flawlessly. The intervening participant2 folder-named-0 problem is a different deployment-specific Drime edge case and is deliberately not spliced into this reporter's causal chain.

solution.intent: Fix Drime multipart destination construction by resolving the configured folder ID to its path from the Drime root and sending the multipart API a root-relative destination path, then ship the change after reporter verification.
solution.concrete_example: For multipart uploads, determine the path from the Drime root to the configured folder ID and prepend it to the requested destination before calling Drime's path-based multipart API. The verified branch was subsequently merged.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter established the size-dependent placement symptom, supplied the object-not-found log, and tested builds. The conclusion that Drime's multipart endpoint interprets its destination as root-relative while rclone had constructed it relative to the configured folder ID came from the maintainer's API and source-code analysis in c2.

edges.comment: Opening report and c1-c3 establish the original reporter's diagnostic chain; c28 provides final pre-landing verification, and c29 records the merge. Medium-size upload reliability reports and the separate folder-named-0 case are not scored as causes of the opening root-placement bug.

solution.intent: Fix Drime multipart destination construction by resolving the configured folder ID to its path from the Drime root and sending the multipart API a root-relative destination path, then request verification on a build containing the change.
solution.concrete_example: The multipart endpoint uses a destination path rather than the folder-ID semantics used by other Drime calls. Resolve the configured folder's full path from root, use that when constructing the multipart destination, and have the reporter verify the same large upload in a test build before declaring it resolved.
solution.inference_hint: This shortcut represents an engineer recognizing the mismatch between folder-ID-relative and root-relative multipart paths directly from the size-dependent placement symptom. Verification is still required before resolution is declared.

edges.comment: Shortcut from the opening state so an agent that immediately proposes the actual multipart path fix can match without first repeating the falsified v1.74.0-only update. It skips the later logs and test-build evidence but must still request user verification.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the root cause of the opening issue: Drime's multipart upload API interprets the destination as a path relative to the account root, while rclone was supplying a path relative to the configured folder ID.
Must fix destination construction by resolving the configured folder ID to its path from the Drime root and using the resulting root-relative path for multipart uploads.
Diagnosis must be grounded in the size-dependent behavior, the completed upload appearing in root with an object-not-found verification error, and the successful placement test on a provided build.
Must not treat installing v1.74.0 or merely reconfiguring the same folder ID as sufficient; both were tried without resolving the issue.
Must not misidentify the transient Cloudflare 520 response or another participant's folder-named-0 edge case as the cause of this reporter's original root-placement problem.
Must ask the reporter to verify a build containing the path fix and only treat the original placement issue as resolved after that verification succeeds.

persona_hint.experience_level: Competent command-line user who can configure rclone remotes, install beta binaries, run verbose copy commands, retry transfers, and provide logs and screenshots, but relies on maintainers for API and source-code diagnosis.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, appreciative, and highly responsive; reports concrete file sizes and command output, tests proposed builds promptly, and raises additional observations when broader testing reveals them.
